name: Dimbong
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Guarisma & Paulian 1986 (comparative/classification) named on Glottolog; no descriptive phonology of Dimbong found.

sources.citation: Guarisma, Gladys. 2003. Kpāʔ (A53). In Nurse & Philippson (eds), The Bantu Languages, 307-334. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Describes Bafia/Kpa (A53, bafi1243), not Dimbong; only lists 'A52 kaaloŋ (rì-péʔ or Mbom)' as a group member (p.307). No statement about Dimbong prosody.

sources.citation: Hyman, Larry M. 2003. 'Abstract' vowel harmony in Kàlòŋ: a system-driven account. In Patrick Sauzet & Anne Zribi-Hertz (eds), Typologie des langues d'Afrique et universaux de la grammaire, vol. 1, 85-112. Paris: L'Harmattan.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; marks only H/L tone ('´ = High tone; ` = Low tone', p.87). CRUCIALLY the paper is not about Dimbong: pp.86-87 identify the language as nù-kàlòŋè 'also known as Yaŋbɛn... Bantu A.62d... spoken in three villages (Yangben, Omendé and Batanga) in the Mbam Division', i.e. Yangben (yang1293), data from Paulian. Glottolog's assignment of this item to dimb1238 is a homonym error (both languages are called 'Kalong').
